diagnostic_evidence.quote:
It is known that continuous maps
between compact Riemannian manifolds are homotopic to HMs (cf.~\cite{EelSam64}).

Thus,  up to translations
there is a unique HM from $\T$ to itself for each homotopy class.

issues.failure_explanation: Compactness alone does not imply this assertion. For example, there is a continuous degree-one map from a torus to the sphere, obtained by collapsing the complement of a disk. It has no harmonic representative for a flat torus and round sphere: a nonzero-degree harmonic torus-to-sphere map must be holomorphic or antiholomorphic, whereas a degree-one such map would be a conformal isomorphism. The source states no additional target hypothesis.

issues.overall_effect: The background theorem and the unrestricted manifold analogy in the abstract and introduction are false. The fractal constructions do not depend on this general assertion.
issues.title: The unrestricted harmonic-representative assertion for compact manifolds is false
issues.why_classification: The source-supported correction abandons the universal claim for compact manifold pairs; it is not a local repair preserving that claim's scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The circle functional sums distances, whereas the lifted functional sums squared differences, so the asserted equality fails even for arbitrarily small edge differences. More decisively, for any nonconstant continuous f choose vertices p,q with distinct images. Every sufficiently fine connected graph has a p-to-q path, whose sum of image distances is at least d_T(f(p),f(q)). Hence the stated circle energy is at least (5/3)^m times a fixed positive number and tends to infinity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the circle energy using squared geodesic distance and justify its eventual equality with the lifted quadratic energy using edge lifts within the injectivity radius of R/Z.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-energy claim and the proposed variational interpretation of nonconstant harmonic maps fail for the functional actually defined.
issues.title: The declared circle energy diverges on every nonconstant map
issues.why_classification: The needed quadratic functional is already the one minimized throughout the construction, so this local correction requires no new optimization scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: Positive definiteness of the matrix of coefficients does not imply nonnegative conductances, nonnegativity of this energy, or strict convexity under boundary anchoring. For example, the positive-definite matrix with diagonal 2 and off-diagonal -1 gives energy -(u1-u2)^2. issues.failure_explanation: Fundamental cycles from a spanning tree can share tree edges. Natural refinement of a shared edge adds new vertices belonging to both refined cycles, contradicting the exact intersection equality. This necessarily occurs in the SG3 example: its level-one graph has 18 edges and 10 vertices, hence nine fundamental cycles and nine tree edges; each cycle uses at least two tree edges, so some tree edge is shared. The advertised natural embedding therefore does not verify the theorem's hypotheses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for the first level of the $n=6$ hexagasket

issues.failure_explanation: This requires all distinct cell pairs to touch, not merely neighboring pairs. It is impossible already for the regular hexagon. Writing the positive contraction ratios as r_i, opposite-pair contact forces r_i+r_(i+3)=1 and hence sum r_i=3. Adjacent-pair contact forces r_i+r_(i+1)+min(r_i,r_(i+1))=1. Summing the latter gives 6 plus a strictly positive quantity equal to 6. Thus the stated construction cannot produce the advertised hexagasket.
